papers.title: Structural and functional modulation of GluA1 AMPA receptor by type I TARP γ4 and type II TARP γ7.
papers.title_zh: I型TARP γ4和II型TARP γ7对GluA1 AMPA受体的结构和功能调节。
papers.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) facilitate fast excitatory neurotransmission, while their dysregulation is associated with neurological conditions, including epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease. AMPARs coassemble with auxiliary subunits, proteins at the periphery of the transmembrane domain that modulate receptor trafficking, localization, and kinetics. The most abundant auxiliary subunits are transmembrane AMPAR regulatory proteins (TARPs), which are subdivided into type I (γ2, γ3, γ4, and γ8) and type II (γ5 and γ7). Here, we used cryo-electron microscopy, electrophysiology, and molecular dynamics simulations to uncover the mechanisms of GluA1 AMPAR modulation by TARPs γ4 and γ7. We find that the divergent effects of γ4 and γ7 are associated with distinct interfaces between TARP extracellular domains and GluA1 ligand-binding domains, driven by structurally distinct extracellular helix orientation and β-sheet architecture. By completing the TARP structural library, this study provides a framework for understanding how different TARP architectures reshape distinct transitions within the AMPAR gating cycle.

papers.title: Allosteric modulation of GluN2B-containing glutamate receptors reduces seizures in autoimmune encephalitis.
papers.title_zh: 含GluN2B的谷氨酸受体的变构调节可减少自身免疫性脑炎的癫痫发作。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (anti-NMDAR) encephalitis manifests with encephalopathy, seizures, cognitive impairment, and sleep disruption that respond poorly to conventional therapies; novel effective treatments are urgently needed. GluN2B-containing NMDARs play important roles in seizure generation and cognition; however, their contribution to anti-NMDAR encephalitis remains unclear. We investigated whether patient-derived anti-NMDAR antibodies alter synaptic GluN1 and GluN2B receptor expression and whether selective GluN2B inhibition affects seizures, memory, and sleep in a mouse model of anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
METHODS: Male C57BL/6 mice (8-12 weeks old, n = 9-11 per group) were continuously infused for 14 days with monoclonal anti-NMDAR antibodies derived from a patient with anti-NMDAR encephalitis or with control IgG. Seizures and sleep were monitored using continuous electroencephalographic recordings. Traxoprodil (10 mg/kg i.p., daily), a selective negative allosteric modulator of GluN2B, was administered throughout the infusion period. Locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, and memory were assessed using open field and object location paradigms. Synaptosomes were isolated from whole brain tissue and were processed for GluN1 and GluN2B protein expression by Western blot.
RESULTS: Consistent with prior studies, 89% of anti-NMDAR antibody-exposed mice developed seizures, with a median of 8 seizures over 2 weeks (interquartile range = 3-18). Antibody-infused mice also demonstrated hippocampus-dependent memory impairment and reduced rapid eye movement (REM) sleep compared to control mice. Traxoprodil diminished seizures (p = .02) but did not alter memory and sleep dysfunction. Anti-NMDAR IgG exposure markedly reduced synaptic GluN1 and GluN2B protein expression, and traxoprodil prevented this (p = .0002 and p = .02, respectively).
SIGNIFICANCE: Our study demonstrates sleep disruption in an animal model of anti-NMDAR encephalitis and highlights the selective role of GluN2B signaling in seizure expression. The persistence of cognitive and sleep disruption during traxoprodil treatment suggests distinct pathophysiological mechanisms. Selective modulation of GluN2B may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for seizure management in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

papers.title: The utility of additional electrodes during stereo-electroencephalography for pediatric epilepsy surgery.
papers.title_zh: 在小儿癫痫手术中进行立体脑电图检查时使用附加电极的实用性。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: There is increasing use of stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) for invasive seizure onset zone (SOZ) localization in children due to its broad, three-dimensional, network-based sampling and improved tolerability compared with other strategies of invasive electrodes. However, initial SEEG does not always result in definitive SOZ localization, and diagnostic yield varies depending on patient selection and institution-specific factors. This study explores the benefits of additional electrodes to define the SOZ during the same hospitalization when initial SEEG sampling is insufficient for surgical planning in children.
METHODS: A cohort of patients who underwent additional electrode placement during the same hospitalization was identified from a database of pediatric epilepsy surgery cases performed between 2015 and 2025. Charts were retrospectively reviewed to obtain variables of interest, including demographics, electrode placement, and surgical outcomes.
RESULTS: Fourteen patients underwent additional electrode placement during the same hospitalization. Reasons for additional electrodes include refining surgical resection margins (50%), inconclusive lobar localization (42%), and inconclusive lateralization (7%). Patients had an average of 11 initial and 3 additional electrode arrays implanted. Patients were monitored for seizure activity on average for 7 days for initial electrodes and an additional 4 days following additional electrode implantation. Following SEEG evaluation, patients underwent either laser ablation (50%), surgical resection (42%), or both (8%). Two patients did not proceed to surgery. Of the 12 patients who underwent surgery, 9 patients (75%) had a most recent follow-up outcome of ILAE 1-3.
CONCLUSIONS: Additional electrode placement during the same hospitalization in this pediatric SEEG cohort was well tolerated with few observed minor complications and is particularly useful when electrodes are added to define surgical margins. Insights from additional electrodes influence subsequent surgical strategy, allowing more limited resections or laser ablations. These findings may contribute to attaining best practices for additional electrode use in pediatric SEEG patients.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Stereotactic electrode placement is being increasingly used to define seizure origin in children with medication-resistant epilepsy, but it can fail to localize seizures in some cases. Placement of additional electrodes during the same hospitalization was associated with few observed minor complications in children and can help refine the surgical plan, allowing for more targeted surgery and may prevent the need for a second epilepsy surgery.

本研究探讨了在初始SEEG采样不足以进行儿童手术规划时，在同一住院期间植入额外电极以确定SOZ的益处。
方法：从2015年至2025年进行的儿童癫痫手术病例数据库中，确定了一组在同一住院期间接受额外电极植入的患者。对病历进行了回顾性审查，以获得变量o
包括人口统计学特征、电极放置和手术结局。
结果：14名患者在同一住院期间接受了额外电极植入。植入额外电极的原因包括：细化手术切除缘（50%）、脑叶定位不确定（42%）以及侧定位不确定（7%）。患者平均植入了11个初始电极阵列和3个额外电极阵列。对患者进行了监测，
对于癫痫发作活动，初始电极平均为7天，额外植入电极后又为4天。在SEEG评估后，患者接受了激光消融（50%）、手术切除（42%）或两者兼有（8%）的治疗。两名患者未接受手术。在接受手术的12例患者中，9例患者（75%）的最近一次随访结果为ILAE 1-3。

papers.title: Development, expert consensus, and pilot feasibility of a school-integrated telehealth model for childhood epilepsy care in India.
papers.title_zh: 针对印度儿童癫痫护理的学校融合远程医疗模式的制定、专家共识和试点可行性。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop, validate through expert consensus, and pilot-test the feasibility of Tele-ESSI (Tele-School Health-led Epilepsy Smart Schools in India), a school-integrated telehealth intervention for childhood epilepsy in resource-limited settings.
METHODS: A multi-phase, mixed-methods intervention development study was conducted across three geographically diverse districts in India. Phase 1 comprised a stakeholder needs assessment through structured workshops, focus group discussions (FGDs), and semi-structured interviews. Phase 2 involved participatory co-design and intervention development, followed by Phase 3, which involved expert validation using a two-round modified Delphi process (consensus threshold: ≥80% agreement; interquartile range ≤1.0). Phase 4 comprised pilot feasibility testing in five purposively selected schools (n = 30 teachers). Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative data underwent thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Three stakeholder workshops (n = 364 participants), FGDs, and in-depth interviews identified system-level gaps in epilepsy literacy, seizure first-aid capacity, and school-healthcare coordination. The resulting Tele-ESSI model integrated three core components: (1) telephonic clinical decision support, (2) structured capacity building, and (3) a multilingual digital integration platform. Fourteen experts completed the modified Delphi process, achieving ≥80% consensus across all domains (mean ratings 8.3-8.8/9). Pilot testing demonstrated high feasibility (4.62 ± 0.30), acceptability (4.44 ± 0.33), usability (4.52 ± 0.38), perceived effectiveness (4.38 ± 0.43), and satisfaction (4.13 ± 0.57). FRAME-guided refinements improved training clarity and digital accessibility.
SIGNIFICANCE: Schools remain underutilized platforms for epilepsy care in low- and middle-income countries, where fragmented health-education coordination contributes to delayed management, stigma, and educational disruption. Tele-ESSI is a stakeholder-informed, consensus-validated, and pilot-tested model that addresses these system-level gaps through integrated clinical support and capacity building within the school setting. Findings support progression to a large-scale effectiveness trial. If effective, the model offers a replicable, scalable, intersectoral framework adaptable to comparable resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Structural deficits, not surgical ones: organizational barriers and a five-stage implementation framework for multidisciplinary epilepsy committees in intermediate-resource centers.
papers.title_zh: 结构性缺陷而非手术性缺陷：中等资源中心的跨学科癫痫委员会的组织障碍和五阶段实施框架。
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), defined by the International League Against Epilepsy as failure of two adequately chosen and tolerated antiseizure medications, affects roughly one-third of people with epilepsy. Epilepsy surgery is the highest-impact therapeutic option for well-selected candidates, yet access depends less on the surgical act itself than on an institutional presurgical pathway and a multidisciplinary team able to identify, study and prioritise candidates in a timely manner. An estimated 10.1 million people with epilepsy are potential surgical candidates, prevalence being highest in Latin America and Africa. In Latin America the mean diagnostic-to-surgery delay is 17.1 years, and in some cohorts only 3.8% of eligible patients reach surgery. This review asks which organisational barriers impede the establishment of a multidisciplinary epilepsy committee in an intermediate-resource public hospital. A structured MEDLINE/PubMed search (2001-2026) combining epilepsy-surgery terms with a mandatory organisational block retrieved 852 records (822 after language limits); screening these plus reference lists yielded 16 included studies, with nine retained purposively as context. Evidence was graded with the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network scheme, barriers categorised with the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, and strategies mapped to the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change. Six barrier domains emerged - referral, workforce, diagnostic infrastructure, technological resources, clinical governance and geographic inequity - operationalised as a five-stage model with paired process and outcome indicators. No included organisational study reached SIGN 1++ or 1+, whereas the surgery being organised rests on randomised evidence: the deficit is structural on both the clinical and evidential axis.

papers.title: Seizure-associated injuries in the United States, 2015 to 2025: a national electronic injury surveillance system analysis.
papers.title_zh: 2015年至2025年美国癫痫发作相关损伤：国家电子损伤监测系统分析。
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the national burden, mechanisms and circumstances, and disposition-based severity correlates of emergency department-treated injuries classified as acute seizure-related in the United States.
METHODS: We searched National Electronic Injury Surveillance System narratives from January 2015 through December 2025 for seizure-related terms, yielding 27,368 candidate records; narrative-based classification identified 22,646 as definitely or probably related to an acute seizure. Cases were assigned to 10 mutually exclusive product/context categories. National estimates and adjusted associations with admission and severe disposition (admission, transfer, or fatality) used survey-weighted analyses accounting for NEISS stratification and clustering.
RESULTS: An estimated 907,778 acute seizure-related injuries occurred over the study period, rising from approximately 70,000 in 2015 to 125,400 in 2025. Home furnishings and flooring accounted for 75.1% of cases; thermal and non-bathroom water/aquatic exposure each accounted for <1%. Status epilepticus (aOR 10.11, 95% CI 6.33-16.16) and alcohol/drug-provoked seizure (aOR 3.06, 95% CI 2.51-3.72) were strongly associated with severe disposition. Non-bathroom water/aquatic exposure was associated with severe disposition in the primary model (aOR 2.40, 95% CI 1.36-4.23) but not after restricting to definite-causation cases. Thermal exposure was not significantly associated with severe disposition.
CONCLUSION: Home furnishings and flooring predominate among seizure-associated emergency department injuries. Status epilepticus and alcohol/drug-provoked seizure carry the strongest association with severe disposition, likely reflecting seizure acuity as well as injury severity. The water/aquatic association is provisional and requires replication. These findings describe emergency department-treated events, not injury incidence among people with epilepsy or per seizure.

papers.title: Understanding psychosis in patients with epilepsy: Insights into demographic, clinical, and treatment-related factors.
papers.title_zh: 了解癫痫患者的精神病：对人口统计学、临床和治疗相关因素的洞察。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although psychosis affects 2%-7% of patients with epilepsy (PWE), its mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify clinical, demographic, electrophysiological, and radiological factors associated with psychosis by comparing PWE with and without psychosis.
METHODS: Medical records of PWE were retrospectively reviewed. The case group (n = 42) comprised PWE with a psychosis, while controls (n = 84) included PWE without psychiatric comorbidity. Demographic, clinical, EEG, and neuroimaging variables were compared between the groups. Factors associated with psychosis in epilepsy were evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression models, with the final multivariate model incorporating clinically relevant and univariately significant variables.
RESULTS: Interictal psychosis was the predominant subtype (57.1%), followed by postictal and ictal psychosis. Univariate analysis showed that lower education, unemployment, longer epilepsy duration, higher number of ASMs, history of status epilepticus (SE), increased seizure frequency, poor adherence, cognitive and neurological abnormalities, background EEG slowing, and hippocampal sclerosis (HS) were significantly associated with psychosis. In the multivariate analysis, higher seizure frequency (OR = 15.31, 95% CI: 5.49-42.72; p < .001), and HS (OR = 3.81, 95% CI: 1.06-13.63; p = .04) remained statistically associated with psychosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Psychosis in epilepsy was associated with a history of SE, higher seizure frequency, poor treatment adherence, and HS in PWE. These findings highlight potentially important clinical associations; however, the retrospective design suggests caution in drawing causal inferences. Early identification of high-risk patients and multidisciplinary collaboration may help optimize patient outcomes and improve clinical management.

papers.title: EEG morphology and peri-ictal MRI abnormalities in status epilepticus and ictal-interictal continuum.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫持续状态和发作间期连续谱中的脑电图形态和发作期MRI异常。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Status epilepticus (SE) is a neurological emergency that may have long-term consequences. Peri-ictal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities (PMAs) may serve as marker of potential acute ictal brain injury and can be used for estimating the risk of SE-defining electroencephalography (EEG) patterns. We hypothesized that excitatory-predominant EEG morphologies reflect higher metabolic demand and a greater likelihood of PMAs than inhibitory-predominant morphologies.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort (February 2019-April 2025), we included patients who had either SE or ictal-interictal continuum (IIC) reported on EEG and underwent acute magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (≤48 h). Excitatory-predominant morphology was defined by a sharp-wave amplitude greater than those of the positive and slow wave, a broad sharp wave (>200 ms), or superimposed fast activity. Inhibitory-predominant morphology was defined by the positive or slow-wave amplitude greater than that of a sharp wave. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between EEG morphology and PMAs on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) or fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR). Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho assessed correlations between the number of excitatory features (0-2) and MRI sequences showing PMAs (none, arterial spin labeling [ASL] hyperperfusion only, or DWI/FLAIR).
RESULTS: Among 205 included patients (134 IIC, 71 SE), excitatory-predominant patterns and lateralized periodic discharges were associated with increased risk of DWI/FLAIR PMAs (p = .001 and p = .02, respectively). In IIC patients, excitatory-predominant morphology was the only predictor of PMAs (p = .002). In the subset with ASL, DWI, and FLAIR sequences (n = 145), the number of excitatory features correlated strongly with types of sequences affected by PMAs (Kendall's tau p < .001; Spearman's rho p < .001).
SIGNIFICANCE: Excitatory-predominant morphology, as opposed to inhibitory-predominant patterns, was associated with a more frequent occurrence of PMAs. These findings support an EEG morphology framework based on excitatory-inhibitory balance across IIC and SE.

papers.title: Analysis of flurothyl-induced seizures and epileptogenesis in mice with targeted deletions of exons 3 and 4 in Dock7.
papers.title_zh: 对Dock7外显子3和4靶向缺失小鼠氟乙基诱导的癫痫发作和癫痫发生机制的分析。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mutations in DOCK7 have been identified in individuals with epileptic encephalopathies. Given that epileptic encephalopathies are a set of disorders that result in seizure activity and associated cognitive and behavioral impairments, we investigated the role of Dock7 in seizure susceptibility and flurothyl kindling using the repeated flurothyl seizure model.
METHODS: Male and female Dock7+/+ and Dock7△ex3-4/△ex3-4 mice (retaining partial Dock7 protein) were subjected to 8 daily flurothyl exposures (kindling; induction phase) followed by a 28-day incubation period and a subsequent flurothyl rechallenge (retest).
RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in baseline latencies to myoclonic jerks or generalized seizures between genotypes or sexes. However, over the kindling period, male Dock7△ex3-4/△ex3-4 mice exhibited slightly longer latencies to myoclonic jerks and generalized seizures (clonic-forebrain seizures) compared to Dock7+/+ males across trials. Female mice showed similar trends, but with no significant differences. Female Dock7△ex3-4/△ex3-4 mice, but not males, showed longer flurothyl-induced generalized seizure durations than female Dock7+/+ mice across the eight induction trials (emerging after trial 2). Following the 28-day incubation period and flurothyl retest, male mice of both genotypes maintained their latencies to generalized seizures upon retest. Dock7+/+ female mice showed increased latencies to myoclonic jerks and generalized seizures during retest, while Dock7△ex3-4/△ex3-4 females maintained their same latencies. Notably, more severe forebrain→brainstem seizures emerged upon flurothyl retest in a significant percentage of mice across all groups. However, the proportion of mice developing this seizure type did not differ significantly between genotypes.
SIGNIFICANCE: Although DOCK7 mutations have been linked to human epileptic encephalopathies and neurodevelopmental dysfunction, we find that overall Dock7△ex3-4/△ex3-4 male and female mice (retaining partial Dock7 protein) do not show heightened excitability or seizure susceptibility using the repeated flurothyl seizure model.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Mutations in the DOCK7 gene have been linked to severe childhood epilepsy. To understand its role, researchers tested whether mice lacking a segment of Dock7 (exons 3-4) were more prone to seizures using repeated exposures to a chemical that can trigger seizures. Mice with this deletion showed no greater seizure susceptibility than wild-type mice. Differences in latencies to seizures between groups were minimal, although sex differences were observed. These findings suggest that loss of a segment of Dock7 alone may not be sufficient to increase seizure susceptibility in mice.

papers.title: Seizure burden and continuity of care among children with epilepsy during Sudan's armed conflict: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
papers.title_zh: 苏丹武装冲突期间癫痫患儿的癫痫发作负担和持续护理：一项多中心横断面研究。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We examined how Sudan's armed conflict changed seizure burden and continuity of care for children on established treatment, and whether the disruptions families described were patterned by conflict exposure or household economic position.
METHODS: Between 26 April and 23 September 2024, clinicians interviewed caregivers of children aged 2-18 years whose epilepsy had been diagnosed before April 2023, recruited from an online pediatric neurology tele-clinic and two eastern teaching hospitals. Care and seizure burden before the war were compared with those at interview using exact McNemar tests. Outcomes were compared between conflict-affected and relatively spared states using prevalence ratios, with Benjamini-Hochberg control of the false discovery rate, and four prespecified multivariable models.
RESULTS: Of 176 interviews, 153 children were analyzed (60.1% male). Follow-up had become irregular for 87 of 152 (57.2%), treatment had been interrupted at least once for 80 of 153 (52.3%), and 66 (43.1%) had lost contact with their physician. The proportion having two or more seizures a month rose from 25.5% to 32.9% (18 deteriorated, 7 improved; exact McNemar p = 0.04). Fifty-six children (36.6%) had a seizure lasting more than 5 min; 34 (60.7%) reached an emergency department immediately and 30 (53.6%) obtained rescue medication. Prolonged seizures (52.1% vs. 28.8%; adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 1.74, 95% CI 1.16-2.63) and irregular follow-up (72.3% vs. 51.0%; aPR 1.45, 95% CI 1.11-1.88) were more frequent in conflict-affected states, but neither unadjusted difference remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons (smallest q = 0.12). Interruption of therapy was determined mainly by household income (lowest two bands, aOR 2.98, 95% CI 1.47-6.04) rather than geography.
SIGNIFICANCE: Epilepsy care in Sudan has been disrupted along the whole pathway and in every region studied. Cost, not distance from the front line, was the dominant barrier to uninterrupted treatment.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Sudan has been at war since April 2023, and we interviewed the families of 153 children who already had epilepsy when the war began. More than half had missed their regular clinic visits, and more than half had run out of their seizure medicine at least once, most often because the family could not afford it. Children living in the states where fighting was taking place were more likely to have long seizures and to miss follow-up, though these differences were not statistically conclusive. Making seizure medicines free would help these children more than any other single measure.

papers.title: Reclassification of deaths reveals underrecognized epilepsy-related mortality in registry data - a retrospective cohort study from a tertiary epilepsy center.
papers.title_zh: 死亡病例的重新分类揭示了登记数据中未被充分认识的癫痫相关死亡率——一项来自三级癫痫中心的病例对照研究。
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Epilepsy-related deaths are underrecognized in registry data due to misclassification or nonspecific coding. We combined national mortality data with systematic case review and research-based reclassification (RBR) to investigate cause-specific mortality in people with epilepsy (PWE).
METHODS: We analyzed causes of deaths in adult PWE population of a tertiary epilepsy center between 1994 and 2021. Logistic regression examined clinical factors associated with epilepsy-related versus non-epilepsy-related causes of death. Survival and standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) were calculated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox models, and population-adjusted life tables.
RESULTS: Among 3,703 PWE (51.2% female; observational period: 48.5 months), 369 (10%) died at a mean age of 57.6 years. Most deaths were non-epilepsy-related (malignancies and cardiovascular diseases; Statistics Austria (SA) 83.2%; RBR 76.2%). Reassessment revealed a significant increase in epilepsy-related mortality (SA 11.9%; RBR 19%, χ2(2)=17.21, p<0.001): 60% occurred during a seizure/status epilepticus (SE), 31.4% were direct seizure consequences, and 8.6% were sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. Epilepsy-related death was associated with early seizure onset (OR 1.04/1.03, p=0.0003/<0.0001, pHolm=0.0094/0.0021 [SA/RBR]), persistent (OR 8.42/5.22, p=0.0038/0.0007, pHolm=0.0956/0.0174) and frequent (OR 14.81/9.96, p=0.0004/<0.0001, pHolm=0.0108/0.0028) seizures, polytherapy (OR 2.29/2.34, p=0.0187/0.0033, pHolm=0.4301/0.0792), history of SE (OR 3.13/3.86, p=0.0015/<0.0001, pHolm=0.0378/0.0005), and comorbidity burden (OR 0.24/0.22, p<0.0001/<0.0001, pHolm=0.0023/<0.0001). Women had lower mortality (HR 0.58, p<0.0001); idiopathic generalized epilepsy carried higher risk than focal epilepsy (HR 1.75, p=0.0064). SMRs were highest in young adults.
CONCLUSION: RBR revealed significantly higher proportion of epilepsy-related deaths, demonstrating that registry data alone underestimates mortality and limits accurate risk estimation and prevention strategies.

papers.title: Clinical scores for predicting functional and neurological outcomes in paediatric status epilepticus: A focused review.
papers.title_zh: 用于预测儿童癫痫持续状态的功能和神经系统结局的临床评分：重点综述。
papers.abstract: Status epilepticus (SE) is a paediatric neurological emergency with outcomes that depend strongly on aetiology and premorbid function. We conducted a focused narrative review of clinical scores evaluated for mortality, refractoriness, or functional outcome in children with SE. Ten primary paediatric reports representing nine distinct cohorts were included in the score-focused synthesis; STEPSS and END-IT reports from India reused the same 140 children. STEPSS performance varied widely across settings, from favourable derivation results to near-chance discrimination in larger retrospective cohorts. PEDSS showed high apparent discrimination in its small derivation cohort, but a later cohort reported poor discrimination for one-year functional decline. END-IT had higher AUCs than STEPSS and mSTEPSS in the only head-to-head comparison; however, it incorporated events occurring during the first 24 h, whereas the other scores used admission variables, and only six deaths occurred. END-IT also performed near chance in an independent PICU cohort. Heterogeneous outcomes, variable score-assessment times, few adverse events and incomplete calibration reporting limit the clinical use of all scores. They may assist exploratory research stratification, but none is validated to determine an individual child's treatment intensity or limitation of care.

papers.title: Clinical cohort study on the prognosis of drug treatment for malformations of cortical development with epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫性皮质发育畸形药物治疗预后的临床队列研究。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Malformations of cortical development (MCD) are a major structural cause of drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Evidence regarding appropriate antiseizure medication (ASM) regimens and prognostic predictors in MCD-related epilepsy remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a real-world retrospective cohort study including 176 patients with MCD-related epilepsy from January 2017 to January 2023. Demographic, clinical, imaging, and treatment data were collected. The primary outcomes were DRE and seizure recurrence after achieving seizure freedom (SF). Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors. Treatment outcomes associated with different ASM strategies were compared.
RESULTS: Of 176 patients, 51.7% developed DRE and 40.9% achieved final SF. Independent risk factors for DRE were first‑line ASM treatment failure within 6 months (HR=3.51, 95%CI: 1.98-6.21, P < 0.001) and dominant hemisphere MCD involvement (HR=1.68, 95%CI: 1.01-2.79, P = 0.047). For seizure recurrence, ASM tapering/discontinuation within 2 years after SF was associated with a higher risk (HR=5.06, 95% CI 1.76-14.56, P = 0.003; Firth HR=4.90, 95% CI 1.72-13.91, P = 0.004). Neurological dysfunction was also associated with recurrence (HR=3.83, 95% CI 1.10-13.27, P = 0.035; Firth HR=3.74, 95% CI 1.04-12.01, P = 0.044) and should be considered exploratory. ASMs monotherapy yielded an SF rate of 61.9%, dual therapy 39.2%, and ≥3 drugs 10.3%. Sodium channel blockers (SCBs) were associated with the highest observed SF rate in the monotherapy subgroup, and the combination of synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) modulators plus SCBs was associated with the highest observed SF rate in the dual-therapy subgroup.
CONCLUSION: For patients with MCD-related epilepsy, SCB monotherapy, as well as the combination of an SV2A modulator with an SCB, was associated with a higher observed SF rate. First-line ASM treatment failure within 6 months was associated with a higher risk of DRE; this subgroup may benefit from consideration of early presurgical evaluation. Among patients with at least 24 months of sustained seizure freedom, ASM tapering or discontinuation within the initial 2‑year period was associated with higher seizure‑recurrence risk.

papers.title: ILAE genetic literacy series: Variant interpretation in epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: ILAE遗传素养系列：癫痫中的变异解读。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract: This article is the first in a two-part primer on variant interpretation in epilepsies, as part of the Genetic Literacy Series by the Genetics Commission of the International League Against Epilepsy. Advances in genetics have significantly improved our understanding of epilepsy, but challenges remain in interpreting the clinical relevance of identified variants. As diagnostic approaches shift from targeted gene panels to broader methods like exome and genome sequencing (ES/GS), the volume of detected variants continues to grow. This primer provides a practical guide to help clinicians navigate variant interpretation, focusing on key aspects such as variant frequency, inheritance, and genotype-phenotype correlations. By equipping clinicians with this knowledge, we aim to improve the integration of genomic testing into routine epilepsy care and enhance patient outcomes. This primer introduces genetic testing strategies, explores the evidence framework for variant interpretation, and concludes by examining common challenges and a case resolution.

papers.title: ILAE Genetics Literacy Series: Epilepsy-associated ion channel disorders.
papers.title_zh: ILAE遗传学知识系列：癫痫相关性离子通道疾病。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract: Ion channel disorders, often referred to as channelopathies, are common among rare disorders, representing the majority of genetic findings in people with monogenic epilepsy syndromes. In total, more than 60 genes encoding ion channels associated with epilepsy have been identified. Establishing the diagnosis of an ion channel disorder has the potential to inform clinical management including candidate precision therapies, thus improving the care of these often severely affected individuals. This review is part of the ILAE Genetics Literacy series and will provide a clinically focused introduction to epilepsy-associated ion channel disorders. We include educational case examples to demonstrate the clinical characteristics, genetic testing, and treatment strategies in these disorders.

papers.title: Outpatient anti-seizure medication tapering following status epilepticus: Clinical predictors and seizure outcomes.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫持续状态后门诊抗癫痫药物减量：临床预测因素和癫痫发作结局。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Management of anti-seizure medications (ASMs) after hospitalization for status epilepticus (SE) is poorly defined, particularly regarding outpatient tapering. We aimed to identify factors associated with ASM tapering and compare seizure recurrence between early and late taper strategies.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of adults hospitalized for SE between 2011 and 2021 with at least 1 year of outpatient follow-up. Statistical analyses included Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable logistic regression to evaluate factors associated with ASM tapering within 1-2 years and seizure recurrence.
RESULTS: Among 282 patients (mean age 55 ± 18 years; 47% female), 37.9% underwent outpatient ASM tapering, of whom 83.7% remained seizure-free for at least 6 months. Early tapering (≤1 year) was associated with higher seizure recurrence compared with late tapering (>1 year) (28.2% vs. 2.7%, p < 0.001). None of eight patients tapered after 2 years experienced recurrence within 6 months. Nonconvulsive SE (odds ratio [OR] 2.21 [1.28-3.84], p = 0.005) and acute symptomatic SE (OR 1.79 [1.01-3.16], p = 0.045) were independently associated with tapering. Most patients who tapered (73.8%) had short SE duration (≤1 day). Acute symptomatic SE was associated with lower 6-months seizure recurrence Odds, approaching significance (adjusted OR 0.27 [0.07-1.03], p = 0.055). Longer SE duration (6-10 days vs. <1 day) was associated with higher odds of recurrence in univariable but not multivariable analysis. SE etiology, number of prehospital ASMs, comorbidities, and outpatient EEG completion were not associated with tapering or recurrence.
SIGNIFICANCE: Despite a relatively low seizure recurrence rate, fewer than 40% of patients underwent ASM tapering. These findings suggest supervised tapering may be reasonable beginning 1 year after SE, particularly in patients with shorter SE duration. Prospective studies are needed to refine tapering strategies.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We reviewed 10 years of medical records from 282 adults hospitalized with status epilepticus to examine when anti-seizure medications were reduced and whether seizures returned. Fewer than 40% had their medications tapered, and most remained seizure-free for at least 6 months. Seizures were more likely to return when medications were reduced within 1 year of hospitalization and less likely following status epilepticus caused by an identifiable trigger, such as a stroke, infection, metabolic disturbance, or missed medication. These findings may help clinicians and patients make more informed decisions about whether and when to reduce anti-seizure medications after status epilepticus.

papers.title: Development of a transition summary and checklist for adolescents with epilepsy using the international classification of functioning, disability and health: a modified Delphi study.

papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transition from pediatric to adult epilepsy care is a complex process that requires coordinated communication and attention to both medical and psychosocial factors. However, standardized tools to support comprehensive information transfer remain limited. This study aimed to develop a structured transition summary and checklist for adolescents with epilepsy, based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF), using a modified Delphi process.
METHODS: A three-stage process comprising a literature review, a two-round modified Delphi study, and a public comment process was conducted. Candidate items were identified through a structured PubMed search, categorized according to ICF domains, and evaluated by a multidisciplinary panel including pediatricians, neurologists, neurosurgeons, allied health professionals, and a family representative. Panelists rated each item for importance and feasibility using a five-point Likert scale. Predefined consensus criteria and weighted scores were used to determine item inclusion and develop the prioritized version.
RESULTS: Of the 53 candidate items, 26 (49.1 %) reached consensus in the first Delphi round, and 46 items reached consensus for inclusion after the second round. The final items covered six domains addressing both medical and psychosocial aspects. Weighted scores, calculated by assigning greater weight to importance than feasibility (2/3 and 1/3, respectively), ranged from 3.6 to 4.8 on a five-point scale.
CONCLUSIONS: An ICF-based transition summary and checklist for adolescents with epilepsy was developed through a structured consensus process. The tool provides a standardized framework for multidisciplinary information transfer between pediatric and adult epilepsy services and may support continuity of care. Future studies should evaluate its usability, implementation feasibility, and clinical impact in real-world clinical settings.

papers.title: Connectivity, receptor architecture and gene expression are associated with brain-wide responses to intracranial electrical stimulation.
papers.title_zh: 连通性、受体结构和基因表达与全脑对颅内电刺激的反应相关。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding how neural activity propagates across brain networks is essential for explaining how focal interventions influence cognition and for guiding neuromodulation strategies. Intracranial electrical stimulation can evoke spatially distributed brain responses, yet the biological factors associated with these response patterns remain poorly understood.
METHODS: We studied 16 epilepsy patients who underwent medial temporal lobe stimulation during concurrent functional magnetic resonance imaging. Whole-brain blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) responses were quantified and related to intrinsic functional connectivity, neurotransmitter principal receptor gradient, and regional gene-expression profiles. Stimulation-evoked electrophysiological responses were examined using an independent cortico-cortical evoked potential (CCEP) dataset for comparison.
RESULTS: Stimulation induced widespread BOLD activation extending beyond the stimulation site, including the insula and middle cingulate cortex. The spatial distribution of BOLD responses was jointly associated with functional connectivity, principal receptor gradient, and gene expression, and could be captured by these biological features in a multivariate model. In contrast, stimulation-evoked electrophysiological responses showed limited spatial correspondence with BOLD responses and were associated with partly different biological features. This suggests that hemodynamic and electrophysiological reactivity capture partly different aspects of stimulation effects.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings link the spatial distribution of stimulation-induced brain responses to functional connectivity, receptor architecture, and transcriptional profiles. Identifying the biological features associated with this spatial variability may help characterize responses to targeted stimulation.

papers.title: Unraveling the interplay between sensory information and semantic architecture in brain concept representation: the role of abstraction.
papers.title_zh: 揭示感官信息与语义结构在大脑概念表征中的相互作用：抽象的作用。
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Understanding how abstract and concrete words are represented in the brain requires disentangling the contribution of sensorimotor information from the organization of semantic knowledge. These dimensions, here referred to as abstractness and abstraction, respectively, are typically confounded, limiting our ability to identify their distinct neural correlates.
OBJECTIVES: The present study aimed to dissociate the roles of abstractness and abstraction in word processing by introducing superordinate words as a critical comparison category.
METHODS: Behavioral norming and feature production tasks were used to quantify sensory-related properties and semantic architecture, operationalized in terms of generalizability, feature relevance, and representational specificity. These measures informed computational models capturing abstractness, abstraction, sensorimotor content, and distributional similarity. Neural data were acquired using electroencephalography and analyzed with representational similarity analysis to assess model-brain correspondence over time.
RESULTS: Behaviorally, superordinate words patterned with concrete words on sensory properties but with abstract words on measures of semantic architecture. In the electrophysiological data, concrete words elicited stronger negativities than both abstract and superordinate words in the N400 and N700 time windows, whereas the contrast between abstract and superordinate words did not reach significance. Representational similarity analysis revealed that, among the models tested, the abstraction model was significantly associated with the neural response patterns in the N400 and N700 latencies, whereas models based on abstractness, sensorimotor or distributional information did not reach the significance threshold.
CONCLUSION: Within the participants and stimuli tested, these results indicate that semantic architecture provides a useful framework for understanding the neural dynamics of word processing, alongside sensorimotor grounding. They suggest that abstraction may play a central role in structuring conceptual representations, providing a unifying account that bridges embodied and formal theories of semantic representation.

papers.title: Task-aware conditional diffusion model for EMG artifact removal in single-channel EEG.
papers.title_zh: 用于单通道脑电图EMG伪影去除的任务感知条件扩散模型。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalography (EEG) is highly susceptible to electromyography (EMG) artifacts, which can obscure task-relevant neural oscillations and degrade downstream analysis. Existing denoising methods usually treat EEG as task-agnostic signals and may attenuate physiologically meaningful rhythms during artifact removal. This study aims to develop a task-aware single-channel EEG denoising framework that suppresses EMG artifacts while preserving task-dependent neural oscillatory characteristics.
APPROACH: We propose TaskEEGDiT, a task-conditioned diffusion framework for EMG artifact removal. The model introduces task-wise spectral prototypes as conditioning signals to guide denoising toward task-relevant spectral distributions, while the noisy EEG is used as a sample-specific reference to constrain the reverse diffusion process and enable deterministic reconstruction. TimeMixer is adopted as the noise prediction backbone to capture non-stationary temporal dynamics and multi-scale dependencies. A multi-constraint joint loss further combines denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) noise prediction, encoder-based temporal content preservation, and power spectral density (PSD)-based spectral style alignment.
MAIN RESULTS: Experiments on motor imagery EEG and sleep EEG datasets show that TaskEEGDiT outperforms tuned baseline models and a task-conditioned DSATCN variant across correlation coefficient, signal-to-noise ratio, spectral-domain relative root mean square error, and time-domain relative root mean square error. TaskEEGDiT achieves SNRs of 13.841 dB and 15.781 dB on the motor imagery and sleep EEG datasets, respectively, improving over DSATCN (task-conditioned) by 2.177 dB and 2.433 dB. Additional analyses across signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels, task conditions, and sleep EEG subjects support robustness, while real-recording results provide preliminary evidence of applicability. With 10-step Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) accelerated sampling, inference time is reduced to 345.684 ms per 2-s EEG segment.
SIGNIFICANCE: TaskEEGDiT demonstrates that task-wise spectral prototype conditioned diffusion modeling can improve EMG artifact removal while limiting alterations to task-relevant EEG spectral characteristics, supporting faster-than-real-time EEG denoising for online brain-computer interface and neurophysiological monitoring scenarios.

papers.title: REALM: Retrospective encoder alignment for LFP modeling.
papers.title_zh: REALM：用于LFP建模的回溯编码器对齐。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Spike activity has been the dominant neural signal for behavior decoding because its high spatial and temporal resolution supports accurate decoding. However, as intracortical brain-computer interfaces (iBCIs) move toward higher channel counts and wireless operation, the high sampling rates required to record spike signals create substantial power and data-bandwidth demands. Local field potentials (LFPs) capture brain activity at a different spatiotemporal scale and offer complementary advantages, including greater long-term stability, reduced energy consumption, and lower bandwidth requirements. Despite these benefits, LFP-based decoding models often achieve lower accuracy and rely on non-causal architectures that cannot be used directly for real-time deployment.
APPROACH: We propose REALM: a retrospective knowledge distillation (RKD) framework for high-performance causal LFP behavior decoding. Inspired by offline-to-online distillation strategies in speech recognition, REALM transfers non-causal representational knowledge learned by a pretrained, multi-session bidirectional LFP teacher to a causal student model for real-time deployment. Specifically, we first pretrain a bidirectional Mamba-2 teacher model across multiple recording sessions using continuous masked autoencoding (CMAE). We then distill its representation into a compact causal student model using a combined objective of representation alignment and autoencoding.
MAIN RESULTS: REALM achieves the highest mean accuracy among the decoders compared, under both linear-probe evaluation and per-session fine-tuning. Its improvements over each baseline, including the state-of-the-art CrossModalDistill, are statistically significant. REALM achieves this performance using a single modality-local field potentials-throughout pretraining, distillation, and decoding, while using less than half as many parameters as CrossModalDistill's published student and requiring one-tenth of the pretraining time.
SIGNIFICANCE: These results demonstrate that REALM effectively bridges the gap between offline and real-time neural decoding. Importantly, REALM shows that a causal LFP-only model can achieve competitive decoding accuracy compared with a non-causal multi-modal model, offering a practical and scalable alternative for next-generation wireless and implantable iBCIs.

papers.title: Emotion recognition oriented to hierarchical brain networks: A contrastive learning-driven novel dual-geometric space framework.
papers.title_zh: 面向分层脑网络的“情绪识别”：一种由对比学习驱动的新型双几何空间框架。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising tool for decoding emotional states and investigating affective disorders. However, existing EEG-based emotion recognition methods often process frequency bands separately and rely on naive feature concatenation, limiting their ability to capture complex nonlinear inter-band interactions. Furthermore, the hierarchical and non-Euclidean nature of cross-band dependencies poses challenges for learning discriminative emotion-related representations. This study aims to address these limitations by developing a hierarchical brain network framework (HBNet) for EEG-based emotion analysis.
APPROACH: HBNet employs a dual-geometric architecture to learn hierarchical EEG representations in Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces. The Band Base Representation (BBR) branch integrates multi-layer residual self-attention with frequency-aware encoding to capture global cross-band dependencies and extract discriminative band-level features. The Band Interaction Enhancement (BIE) branch employs cross-band attention to model inter-band correlations and integrate complementary information, followed by hyperbolic mapping to characterize hierarchical cross-band relationships. Additionally, Dual-Geometric Cross-Band Contrastive Learning (DGCB-CL) is introduced to align representations across the two geometric spaces while preserving their respective geometric properties, thereby enhancing feature discrimination and generalization.
MAIN RESULTS: Extensive experiments on public EEG emotion recognition datasets demonstrate that HBNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of the proposed dual-geometric architecture and cross-band representation learning strategy.
SIGNIFICANCE: HBNet provides a framework for modeling complex cross-band dependencies in EEG signals by integrating Euclidean and hyperbolic representations with contrastive learning. It offers a potential approach for analyzing emotion-related brain activity and may support further investigations into the neural mechanisms of affective disorders and their auxiliary assessment. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/cvmdsp/HBNet.

papers.abstract: We tested whether decoder posteriors identify failed motor-imagery (MI) brain-computer interface sessions without trustworthy intent labels. The monitor is target-label-free but source-supervised: historical cohorts provide training labels; monitored sessions and cohorts do not. Each subject-specific decoder uses the participant's labelled calibration data.Approach.We analysed 38,733 trials in 190 held-out sessions from 181 participants across five public cohorts, treating participants as resampling clusters. Common spatial patterns and linear discriminant analysis (CSP-LDA) provided decoder posteriors. A nested leave-one-dataset-out ridge monitor predicted chance-normalized balanced accuracy $S$ from posterior summaries. Comparators included confidence-based estimators, normalized decoder-outputinformation $I_{\mathrm{out}}$ and cue-labelled prefix accuracy. Post hoc analyses tested command priors, class substitution, calibration and source-selected alarm cutoffs.Main results.The full monitor achieved mean absolute error 0.124 and dataset-stratified failure ($S<0.20$) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.883 (95\% confidence interval 0.826-0.930); a count-free variant achieved 0.117 and 0.872. $I_{\mathrm{out}}$ alone reached AUROC 0.877. From 20 trials, output information and labelled prefix accuracy had future-failure AUROCs of 0.852 and 0.842; non-inferiority was not established.For the full monitor without a gate, a cutoff targeting 90% source sensitivity yielded 0.932 target sensitivity and 0.644 specificity. At 90% command dominance, mean information decreased by 31.8%, AUROC changed from 0.879 to 0.861, and false alarms rose from 34 to 37. Information retained discrimination under temperature scaling but was unchanged by systematic class substitution.Significance.CSP-LDA posteriors carry session-level failure risk. Cue labels remain preferable for point estimation. Consistent transfer to Riemannian minimum-distance to-mean posteriors was not established; online and asynchronous validity remain untested.

papers.title: STRIDE: A Flexible, Depth-Controlled Intramuscular EMG Platform for Small-Animal Studies.

papers.iso_journal: IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng
papers.abstract: Reliable electromyography (EMG) recording can substantially improve closed-loop neuromodulation workflows by providing timely feedback on muscle recruitment. Conventional EMG needles limit intramuscular EMG recordings through placement variability, motion sensitivity, and inconsistent SNR. We introduce STRIDE (Stable Targeted Recording, Intramuscular Depth-controlled Electromyography), a flexible printed-circuit array with depth stops and selectable cross- and down-fiber bipolar pairings. In vivo in the mouse hindlimb, we compared STRIDE to EMG needles during non-selective sciatic electrical stimulation and physiological toe-pinch. Arrays were implanted at mid-belly using the depth stop and verified post-hoc by micro-computed tomography. Within a single muscle, STRIDE recordings produced lower baseline noise and higher SNR than the needle, despite the needle's larger compound muscle action potential amplitude. Frequency spectra showed reduced line and broadband interference on STRIDE channels. Concurrent recordings from four muscles in a mouse hind limb at identical stimulation amplitudes revealed a tibial-leaning recruitment profile at maximal drive, consistent with branch anatomy and array placement. During physiological toe-pinch, artifactcontrolled analysis showed that STRIDE captured more array-level event times than the single bipolar needle channel and yielded two to three recurring waveform classes per STRIDE channel, supporting broader multi-site sampling of putative physiological EMG activity. Furthermore, STRIDE required no reinsertions, whereas the needles required many. STRIDE also exhibited higher axial retention, and landed within the intended depth-stop increment, supporting depth-guided and stable implantation in this study. STRIDE provides a more stable, multi-site intramuscular high-density EMG recording platform and, in this acute comparison, achieved improved practical SNR consistent with contributions from recording geometry and reduced baseline noise beyond raw amplitude alone. Our platform supports multi-muscle readouts for neuromuscular physiology, mapping, and future closed-loop applications.

papers.title: State-dependent gating of sensory and cortical inputs by median raphe neurons.
papers.title_zh: 中缝核神经元对感觉和皮层输入的“状态依赖性”门控。
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: The mesopontine median raphe (MnR) plays an important role in regulating brain states, hippocampal network activity, and memory processes. Recent studies have revealed that the MnR comprises three major neuronal populations: serotonergic (5-HT), glutamatergic (Vglut3-expressing), and GABAergic neurons. How these distinct neuronal populations may gate sensory and cortical inputs across different brain states remains largely unknown. Here, we combined in vivo electrophysiological recording, sensory or optogenetic stimulation, and transgenic approaches to characterize the response properties of 5-HT, Vglut3, and GABAergic MnR neurons during wakefulness and sleep. We found that MnR neurons exhibited pronounced state-dependent responses to both sensory and cortical stimulation, with response amplitudes significantly greater during slow-wave sleep than during wakefulness. Auditory and somatosensory stimuli elicited fast responses in the MnR: 5-HT neurons were primarily suppressed, whereas Vglut3 and GABAergic neurons were primarily activated, suggesting the presence of direct inputs from sensory thalamic or brainstem structures. Retrograde tracing identified several brainstem structures and, notably, the medial prefrontal cortex as sources of direct projections to the MnR. Optogenetic stimulation of prefrontal inputs to the MnR evoked inhibition of 5-HT neurons but robust excitation of Vglut3 neurons during slow-wave sleep, suggesting top-down control of MnR activity by the prefrontal cortex. Together, these findings reveal that the MnR exhibits enhanced sensitivity to both ascending sensory and descending cortical inputs during sleep, suggesting that it may integrate environmental and cortical signals to regulate hippocampal network activity and gate sleep-dependent memory processing.

papers.title: Multiloop Feedback Model of Metabolic-Blood Flow-Electrical Activity Coupling and Its Potential for Closed-Loop Regulation.

papers.abstract: The brain's physiological function depends on tightly coupled interactions among neural activity, metabolism, and cerebral blood flow (CBF), involving interconnected processes of neurovascular and neurometabolic coupling (NMC). While previous studies have often examined these relationships within individual regulatory pathways, growing evidence suggests that their interactions across multiple spatial and temporal scales may contribute to the maintenance of energy homeostasis and neural stability. This review synthesizes the physiological foundations of metabolic-hemodynamic-electrical coupling and reviews emerging modeling and imaging approaches for characterizing these interactions, including dynamic fluid-reaction-diffusion (DFRD) modeling, photoacoustic and two-photon imaging (2PM), and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). A central focus of this review is a conceptual closed-loop framework in which metabolic and blood-flow variables could be incorporated into neuromodulation objectives alongside neural activity, with the potential to jointly consider therapeutic efficacy, metabolic burden, and neurovascular state. Key methodological, technical, and translational challenges are discussed, including multimodal data integration, temporal and spatial alignment, model identifiability, computational efficiency, and experimental validation. Future directions toward personalized and metabolism-aware neural interfaces are also outlined. This article is a narrative review with a forward-looking conceptual framework; it does not report original simulations, controller benchmarking, or clinical validation.

papers.title: Ascending somatosensory systems processing affiliative social touch.
papers.title_zh: 处理亲密性社交触摸的上行躯体感觉系统。
papers.abstract: Affiliative social touch is a fundamental channel of mammalian communication that influences attachment, parenting, social buffering, play, and reproduction. Traditionally, somatosensory research focused on discriminative properties of touch, while later studies emphasized affective touch mediated by C-tactile afferents and related pathways. Here, we propose a broader framework in which affiliative social touch is understood not as a specialized affective modality but as a multidimensional social signal whose meaning depends on context, internal state, social relationship, and behavioral goals. Drawing primarily on rodent models, we review the ascending somatosensory systems that convey affiliative tactile information from the periphery to the brain. We discuss the contributions of low-threshold mechanoreceptors, the vibrissal system, and also spinal circuits that begin transforming tactile signals into affectively relevant representations. We further examine parallel ascending pathways through the brainstem, thalamus, and cortex, highlighting the roles of the parabrachial nucleus, posterior intralaminar thalamic nucleus, hypothalamic and limbic networks, and cortical systems involved in sensory processing, salience detection, and social cognition. Neuromodulatory systems, including oxytocin, endogenous opioids, dopamine, and serotonin, which shape the behavioral interpretation of affiliative social touch are also discussed. Finally, we consider the conservation of these mechanisms in human. The paper argues that affiliative social touch is not encoded by dedicated pathways for specific social behaviors; rather, common somatosensory signals gain social meaning through interactions with distributed neural circuits and state-dependent modulatory mechanisms. Understanding how ascending somatosensory pathways transform affiliative social contact into socially meaningful representations provides a unifying framework for investigating the neural basis of social behavior.

papers.title: AI-Driven Non-Invasive Scalp EEG Biosensing for Real-Time Seizure Prediction Using Lightweight Gradient Boosting Ensembles.
papers.title_zh: 使用轻量级梯度提升集成算法，通过人工智能驱动的无创头皮脑电生物传感实现实时癫痫发作预测。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of non-invasive scalp electroencephalography (EEG) seizure prediction is severely hindered by patient-dependency, elevated false alarm rates, and excessive computational latency. This study introduces a computationally lightweight, patient-independent machine learning pipeline designed to achieve cross-patient generalization and robust false alarm suppression without requiring subject-specific calibration.
METHODS: Using the continuous multi-channel scalp EEG dataset from the CHB-MIT benchmark (materials/setting), signals underwent dual-stage filtering (1-70 Hz bandpass, 60 Hz notch), artifact removal via Extended FastICA, and Common Average Referencing. Dimensionality was reduced via Principal Component Analysis (12 orthogonal components, >95.4% variance explained). Continuous streams were partitioned into 5 s sliding windows (90% overlap) to extract multi-domain temporal, spectral, and discrete wavelet features, subsequently pruned via ANOVA F-testing to 168 salient predictors. Pre-ictal transitions (20 to 5 min prior to seizure onset, incorporating an excluded 5 min prediction horizon buffer) were classified using a synchronized ensemble of regularized XGBoost and leaf-wise LightGBM models. Dual-model coincidence was governed by a 30 s moving temporal alignment window coupled with 12-epoch persistence smoothing and a 30 min refractory lockout. To prevent intra-subject data leakage, multi-session recordings from the same individual (Cases 01 and 21) were strictly co-located within the training set, and the pipeline was evaluated on an isolated cohort of four completely unseen subjects (Patients 20, 22-24) across 156.5 continuous, unsampled hours.
RESULTS: On the independent unseen test cohort, the post-processed framework achieved a primary event-level seizure sensitivity of 100% (34/34 seizures detected; 95% Clopper-Pearson CI: 89.72-100.0%), mathematically bounded by the test sample size, with a false alarm rate of 0.415/h (an 89.5% reduction versus the raw ensemble) and a mean Seizure Prediction Horizon of 17.03 min. Under continuous 0.5 s sliding-window streaming (designed for real-time edge persistence filtering), the framework demonstrated 99.80% operational pre-ictal alert consistency (60,772/60,894 sliding windows; specificity: 98.64%, precision: 91.20%, F1-score: 95.31%). Evaluated on strictly independent, non-overlapping 5 s epochs (N = 6120), the ensemble retained a pre-ictal sensitivity of 99.1%, confirming robust performance independent of window overlap. Execution latency was 0.0057 ms per window, delivering a >1000× speedup over state-of-the-art 3D-CNN and Transformer architectures.
CONCLUSIONS: By eliminating multi-session data leakage and mitigating clinical alarm fatigue, this pipeline offers reliable cross-patient generalizability, practical intervention timing, and ultra-low computational latency suitable for real-time deployment on low-power wearable closed-loop neurostimulation devices.

papers.title: Proprioception and Sensorimotor Control After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Non-Invasive Peripheral Neuromodulation and Neurorehabilitation Technologies.
papers.title_zh: 中风后的本体感觉和感觉运动控制：对非侵入性外周神经调节和神经康复技术的系统综述。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Proprioceptive impairment can limit recovery after stroke, yet functional gains may be mistaken for sensory recovery. This systematic review evaluated non-invasive vibratory and peripheral or afferent electrical stimulation targeting proprioception, kinesthetic perception, sensorimotor processing, and neurorehabilitation technologies.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, we synthesized 38 publications: 33 primary empirical studies spanning clinical, mechanistic, and technological research, and five secondary reviews (three systematic/meta-analytic and two narrative/technical). Historical search records were incompletely recoverable. Evidence was classified by design and outcome domain, distinguishing direct proprioceptive assessments, neurophysiological correlates, and motor or functional outcomes. Methodological quality was appraised using design-specific tools.
RESULTS: Direct proprioceptive assessment was uncommon. Focal and whole-body vibration, afferent electrical stimulation, neuromuscular and functional electrical stimulation, and technology-assisted approaches showed variable effects on kinesthetic perception, cortical activity, balance, gait, and motor performance. However, motor and functional gains did not consistently coincide with measurable proprioceptive recovery. Among 15 parallel-group randomized trials, eight raised some concerns and seven were judged at high overall risk of bias.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence supports possible sensorimotor effects of peripheral neuromodulation but cannot establish an optimal protocol for proprioceptive restoration. Future controlled trials should jointly measure proprioception, neurophysiological responses, and functional outcomes, including retention and transfer.

papers.title: Neural State Geometry: Unifying Amplitude Landscapes, Coherency Geometry and Information Geometry for EEG State Estimation.
papers.title_zh: 神经状态几何：统一振幅景观、相干性几何和信息几何，用于脑电图状态估计。
papers.abstract: Brain-state engineering requires measurement and modulation through interpretable, physics-informed coordinates of EEG state structure, change and intervention response. Applications include cognitive fatigue monitoring, neuromodulation readout and progress toward adaptive closed-loop neurotechnology. We introduce Neural State Geometry (NSG), which is a sensor-space framework derived from the complex analytic EEG field rather than a biophysical neuronal model. NSG integrates a Neural Amplitude Landscape (NAL), mapping analytic-amplitude distributions to statistical temperature, internal energy, entropy and heat capacity through exact canonical statistical thermodynamics; pairwise Stokes/coherency geometry representing inter-channel organisation using electromagnetic coherence theory; and quantum-information-inspired state-space geometry quantifying selected-basis organisation. We evaluate NSG through controlled synthetic tests, outcome-blind human-EEG amplitude-model comparison, a single-participant cognitive fatigue example, and a single-investigator transcranial focused ultrasound (TUS) neuromodulation feasibility case. Synthetic tests established descriptor selectivity and common-source sensitivity of zero-lag second-order geometry. NAL/generalised-gamma improved participant-balanced held-out prediction over Rayleigh, Nakagami and gamma but not lognormal. The cognitive fatigue example showed predominantly positive PRE-POST NAL shifts with spectral and second-order deformation. In the fixed-order TUS case, the largest reference-stable NAL displacement occurred at the application site alongside broader sensor-space deformation. NSG provides an interpretable layer for comparing natural and intervention-associated EEG states, supporting future biomarker and target-engagement validation, mechanistic investigation and closed-loop neural engineering.

papers.title: Task exposure and stimulation duration modulate HD-tDCS effects on working memory in older adults.
papers.title_zh: 任务暴露和刺激持续时间调节HD-tDCS对老年人工作记忆的影响。
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Age-related working-memory decline has been associated with altered neural oscillations, and high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) may improve cognition. However, responses vary and may depend on prior task engagement and stimulation duration.
METHODS: We examined these factors in a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover study of 39 healthy older adults (65.4 ± 3.0 years). Participants received real and sham 2-mA HD-tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for 10 or 20 min. Task exposure before real stimulation was determined by stimulation sequence, creating less- and more-exposure groups. Working-memory performance and EEG spectral power were assessed during two-back tasks before and after stimulation.
RESULTS: Change in discrimination sensitivity (Δd') showed a Stimulation × Duration × Exposure interaction. Exploratory comparisons indicated that 10-min real stimulation improved Δd' relative to sham in the less-exposure group but reduced Δd' in the more-exposure group; neither 20-min subgroup showed a significant effect. Secondary inverse-efficiency analyses showed improved efficiency after real stimulation under less exposure and poorer efficiency under more exposure. The more-exposure, 10-min group also showed increased central beta power following real stimulation. Associations between beta-power changes and poorer behavioral performance did not remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that HD-tDCS effects vary with stimulation duration and prior task context. However, the small subgroups and confounding of task exposure with stimulation order and session position require cautious interpretation. Larger studies independently manipulating exposure and stimulation order are needed to confirm these potentially state-dependent effects.

papers.title: Spasmodic Dysphonia and Muscle Tension Dysphonia: A Review of Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Evidence.
papers.title_zh: 痉挛性发音障碍和肌张力性发音障碍：神经影像学和神经生理学证据综述。
papers.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Spasmodic dysphonia (SD), or laryngeal dystonia (LD), and muscle tension dysphonia (MTD) are clinically overlapping voice disorders with different positions in current pathophysiological models. This review synthesizes multimodal neuroimaging and neurophysiological evidence on their central mechanisms, compares the implicated neural systems, and assesses whether such measures can aid future differential diagnosis.
METHODS: A structured search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, and Google Scholar (final search, March 29, 2026), limited to English-language publications from January 2000 through March 2026 and supplemented by reference-list screening and forward citation tracking. Evidence was synthesized across task-based and resting-state fMRI, structural MRI and morphometry, diffusion tensor and kurtosis imaging, PET, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), and magnetoencephalography. Studies were appraised qualitatively for design, sample size, diagnostic phenotype, comparator groups, treatment or botulinum toxin washout status, findings, and limitations.
RESULTS: The SD/LD literature provided relatively consistent evidence of abnormalities across distributed voice-control networks involving cortical, subcortical, cerebellar, and brainstem systems, recurring in primary sensorimotor cortex, supplementary and premotor regions, inferior frontal and parietal cortices, insula, putamen, thalamus, cerebellum, and their white-matter connections. Some abnormalities persisted outside phonation or before movement onset, supporting a trait-like component; TMS showed impaired cortical inhibition and a shortened cortical silent period (CSP) in SD/LD. The MTD evidence base remained limited, comprising one case-control task-fMRI study of ten women, one single-patient pre-/post-treatment fMRI study, and one TMS study with an MTD comparator. These findings suggested possible central involvement but did not establish a causal mechanism, a stable MTD-specific network, or the contributions of compensation, state-dependent effects, and phonatory effort; comparable CSP shortening was not reported in MTD.
CONCLUSIONS: SD/LD is best understood as a distributed disorder of central voice-control networks, whereas MTD appears to be a hyperfunctional voice disorder with plausible but incompletely characterized central influences. Unequal evidence volume should not be read as established biological divergence, and the "neurological" versus "non-neurological" distinction remains provisional. Imaging and physiological measures are not yet validated biomarkers, and CSP is only a candidate marker pending replication and validation. Larger, clinically stratified, harmonized multimodal head-to-head studies are needed, potentially integrating neural, physiological, acoustic, and clinical measures for reliable differential diagnosis.

papers.title: Adaptive Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation in Parkinson's Disease: Results and Learnings from a Consecutive, Real-World Cohort.
papers.title_zh: 帕金森病患者的自适应丘脑底核深部脑刺激：来自连续性真实世界队列的结果和经验教训。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS)-automatically modulating amplitude based on local field potential (LFP) activity -is a promising alternative to continuous amplitude DBS delivery (cDBS). Data on its efficacy and safety in real-world conditions are scarce.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of the study was to report on the initial experience with alpha-beta (8-30 Hz)-guided subthalamic nucleus (STN) aDBS in Parkinson's disease (PD) in a single-center cohort.
METHODS: PD patients were consecutively enrolled after STN DBS surgery, had traditional cDBS programming postoperatively, and were systematically reviewed at 3 months (initial LFP-guided cDBS setup), 6 months (preadaptive setup), 7 months (aDBS initiation), 8-9 months (short-term visit), and 10-13 months (medium-term visit). Clinical, neurophysiological, and patient perception data were collected.
RESULTS: Of 18 patients (34 hemispheres) who were switched to aDBS, 17 and 15 remained on aDBS at the short-term and medium-term time points, respectively. aDBS was comparable to cDBS in most outcomes, and better outcomes were observed on motor fluctuations (Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale [MDS-UPDRS] Part IV-1.5 points, P = 0.02) and quality of life (39-item Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire [PDQ-39] Summary Index-1.4 points, P = 0.01) compared to LFP-guided cDBS. After aDBS setup, an 80% patient-reported improvement was observed in symptoms persisting on cDBS (mainly gait problems, tremor, and dyskinesia). LFP peak frequency remained stable over time.
CONCLUSIONS: aDBS was safe, feasible, preferred by patients, and clinically comparable to optimized cDBS for most outcomes in a consecutive, unblinded cohort, providing additional benefits on motor fluctuations and quality of life. A systematic approach in selecting the LFP band and thresholds pre-aDBS and programming settings post-aDBS is recommended.

papers.title: The what, how and where of statistical learning: a neurocognitive synthesis.
papers.title_zh: 统计学习的“什么”、“如何”和“在哪里”：神经认知综合。
papers.abstract: The ability to learn environmental regularities - statistical learning - is crucial for language, cognition and behaviour. Despite decades of research, fundamental questions remain about what statistical learning is, how the mind supports it and where in the brain it is implemented. We address these questions with a framework based on Marr's levels of analysis. At the 'what' level, we suggest that statistical learning is best defined in terms of its goal: to learn latent structure in the input across repeated exposures. We focus on three widely studied sequential statistical learning tasks that embody this definition: embedded pattern, artificial grammar and serial reaction time tasks. At the 'how' and 'where' levels, our comprehensive reviews reveal that sequential statistical learning depends on at least two cognitive learning processes (prediction-based learning and chunking) and two well-established neural learning circuits (rooted in the basal ganglia and the medial temporal lobe). We describe empirically motivated 'many-to-many' mappings between the tasks, learning processes and neural circuits that integrate the three levels. Further, we suggest that task, input and learner characteristics can shift the relative reliance on these processes and circuits. Overall, our synthesis elucidates the cognitive and neural substrates of sequential statistical learning and provides predictions to guide future research.

papers.title: Rewiring cancer: peripheral nerves control tumours.
papers.title_zh: 重塑癌症：外周神经控制肿瘤。
papers.abstract: The peripheral nervous system has emerged as an important regulator of cancer biology. Once considered passive bystanders, tumour-infiltrating neurites are now recognized as active components of the tumour microenvironment that influence tumour progression through direct and indirect interactions with malignant, immune, stromal, glial and vascular cells. Recent studies have demonstrated that peripheral tumours recruit and remodel infiltrating neurites, inducing transcriptional, structural and functional changes that resemble neural injury and regenerative programs. These reprogrammed neurites release neurotransmitters, neuropeptides and other factors that directly promote tumour cell proliferation, migration and survival while reshaping the surrounding microenvironment. Neural signalling influences antitumour immunity, reprogrammes fibroblasts and promotes angiogenesis, collectively generating conditions that support disease progression. In turn, tumour-associated neurites undergo profound alterations in their connectivity, activity and molecular state, highlighting the dynamic and reciprocal nature of tumour-nerve interactions. These discoveries have reshaped our understanding of how pro-tumorigenic microenvironments are established and maintained. Importantly, defining the molecular pathways that mediate neural regulation of cancer has revealed new therapeutic opportunities, including the potential repurposing of FDA-approved agents that target neural signalling pathways. As the field of cancer neuroscience continues to advance, the nervous system is increasingly recognized not only as a regulator of tumour behaviour but also as a promising target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: The aging brain and epilepsy: Current knowledge and novel therapeutic targets.
papers.title_zh: 衰老的大脑和癫痫：当前知识和新型治疗靶点。
papers.abstract: The prevalence and incidence of unprovoked seizures and epilepsy markedly increase in older populations, most commonly secondary to cerebrovascular disease or neurodegenerative processes such as Alzheimer disease. This late-onset epilepsy (LOE) carries unique clinical challenges, including altered drug metabolism and drug efficacy. Despite this, animal models of aging are rarely included in the preclinical development of novel antiseizure medications (ASMs). Here, we provide a comprehensive perspective on the basic and cellular physiology and pharmacology underlying LOE pathogenesis and treatment. Aged rodents exhibit profoundly altered seizure susceptibility, including an increased vulnerability to focal seizures and epileptogenesis caused by physiological changes in the aging brain. Despite this, both aged rodents and older patients demonstrate an increased sensitivity to the anticonvulsant effects of several established ASMs. We highlight how this enhanced efficacy is driven not only by pharmacokinetic alterations but also by complex pharmacodynamic shifts, including altered GABAA and glutamate receptor subunit composition, ion channel modifications, and compensatory network adaptations. These occur on the background of neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and the accumulation of senescent cells, all emerging therapeutic targets in the epilepsy. Finally, this review explores the intersection of Alzheimer disease and epilepsy, and evaluates the potential of newer experimental therapeutic pathways, including mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibition, senolytics, sirtuin activators, and blood-brain barrier protection. By integrating basic cellular mechanisms with preclinical in vivo data, this review emphasizes the urgent need to incorporate aged animal models in ASM discovery pipelines to successfully identify novel therapies for the treatment of LOE and tailor treatments for the aging brain. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE) is the third most common neurological disorder in older people after stroke and dementia and is often associated with high cognitive, psychological, and psychosocial comorbidity burden and frailty, however, has received comparatively little attention. This review evaluates animal models for LOE, assesses the neurobiological mechanisms of the aged brain's increased sensitivity to seizures and epilepsy, and discusses current and potential novel therapeutic targets, providing a vital resource for advancing LOE research and improving therapeutic approaches.
